column1: When (4.37) is interpreted as a budget constraint that must be satisfied for all price levels, that is, under Ricardian policies, any decision to cut taxes today (and so lower the right side of (4.37)) must be accompanied by planned future tax increases to leave the right side unchanged. In standard infinite-horizon, representative-agent models, a tax cut (current and future government expenditures unchanged) has no e¤ect on equilibrium (i.e., Ricardian equivalence holds) because the tax reduction does not have a real wealth e¤ect on private agents. Agents recognize that in a Ricardian regime, future taxes have risen in present value terms by an amount exactly equal to the reduction in current taxes.
